content.sentence: The mechanic __________ the hydraulic lift without securing the car properly, and the vehicle almost slipped off.
Yesterday, the supervisor __________ the main battery after noticing a burning smell near the alternator.
__________ the technician __________ the emergency brake when the car rolled forward unexpectedly?
The trainees __________ the fuel leak on the workshop floor, and the fumes spread dangerously close to the welding area.
The assistant __________ the coolant hoses loosely, and hot coolant sprayed across the engine bay.
Last night, Ruwan __________ a temperature warning from the radiator, and the engine overheated badly.
__________ you __________ the jack stands properly before going under the vehicle?
The supervisor __________ the trainees away from the vehicle when the fuel injector line burst.
They __________ the exposed wiring near the engine block, and sparks started flying.
When the brake system failed during the test run, the technician __________ the ignition immediately to stop the vehicle.
__________ the fire extinguisher __________ correctly when you tried to control the small engine fire?
The trainee __________ the heavy wheel nuts firmly, and one wheel detached during the diagnostic run.

activity_b.text: The mechanic used the hydraulic lift without securing the car properly, and the vehicle almost slipped off.
Yesterday, the supervisor shut off the main battery after noticing a burning smell near the alternator.
Did the technician press the emergency brake when the car rolled forward unexpectedly?
The trainees didn’t clean the fuel leak on the workshop floor, and the fumes spread dangerously close to the welding area.
The assistant attached the coolant hoses loosely, and hot coolant sprayed across the engine bay.
Last night, Ruwan didn’t hear a temperature warning from the radiator, and the engine overheated badly.
Did you check the jack stands properly before going under the vehicle?
The supervisor warned the trainees away from the vehicle when the fuel injector line burst.
They didn’t repair the exposed wiring near the engine block, and sparks started flying.
When the brake system failed during the test run, the technician cut the ignition immediately to stop the vehicle.
Did the fire extinguisher work correctly when you tried to control the small engine fire?
The trainee didn’t tighten the heavy wheel nuts firmly, and one wheel detached during the diagnostic run.

activity_c.text: Good morning, everyone. I’m glad you’re all here on time.
Today, I want to talk to you about handling some of the more serious emergencies that can occur on the workshop floor.
These situations are not meant to scare you, but to help you stay safe and confident while you work.
A few of these incidents happened last term, so it’s good for us to learn from them and do better next time.
Let’s start with the industrial steamers.
Always take a moment to check the pressure gauge before you begin.
Last month, one group didn’t follow the checklist properly, and the steamer released hot steam all of a sudden.
No one was seriously hurt, but it created a lot of stress.
So please follow the checklist, watch the gauge, and let someone know if you hear anything unusual.
Early warning signs are important.
This morning, we noticed a possible gas leak, so the maintenance team is working on it right now.
If this ever happens while you’re around, don’t switch on any electrical device and step away from the area.
Then inform a supervisor as soon as you can.
Gas leaks can be risky, but when we respond calmly and quickly, everything stays under control.
Another point I want to highlight is the safe handling of chemicals.
Sometimes students mix cleaning products without realising how strong they are.
Last week, someone accidentally mixed two powerful sanitisers, and the fumes irritated people’s eyes.
So when you’re working with chemicals, wear gloves, open the windows, and follow the instructions on the label.
These simple steps keep everyone comfortable and safe.
We also need to pay attention to electrical safety.
Yesterday, a damaged cable was left near the chiller, and the student who noticed it didn’t report it.
It’s an easy thing to miss, but exposed wires can become serious very quickly.
If you ever see something like that, just switch off the machine, move back, and inform the instructor.
A quick report can prevent a big problem.
While some of you are practising with the large mixer today, please remember to keep your hands away from the moving parts and use the safety guard.
The guard may seem small, but it does an important job.
In any emergency—fire, chemical spill, injury, or equipment trouble—try to stay calm, help each other, and look for the evacuation path immediately.
We’re here to learn, but we’re also here to look out for one another.
That’s what makes a workshop safe and supportive.
